Selecting the best of six configurations on the same validation users creates winner’s optimism: the winning gain partly reflects favorable noise. Report all configurations, category scores, macro gains, and the complete search scope, including checkpoint selection; call results exploratory. Independent evaluation or nested evaluation separates selection from assessment ([Cawley–Talbot](https://jmlr.org/papers/volume11/cawley10a/cawley10a.pdf)). For six prespecified baseline comparisons, Holm-adjusted tests or simultaneous bootstrap intervals can address multiplicity under their assumptions; they do not remove optimism from the winning point estimate or cover undisclosed adaptive searches ([Romano–Wolf](https://doi.org/10.1198/016214504000000539)).

For descriptive uncertainty, resample 200 users with replacement within each category, preserving each user’s baseline/configuration hit indicators together, then average the four category mean differences equally. This paired, category-stratified bootstrap preserves comparison pairing and macro weighting. Interpretation is conditional on trained models, fixed categories, and sampled candidates, assuming users are suitable independent sampling units. It excludes training randomness, candidate-draw variation, and generalization to new datasets. Bootstrapping only the selected winner does not provide selection-adjusted coverage; reselection within bootstrap samples alone supplies no independent confirmation. Fixed candidates improve comparability, but sampled HR@10 need not preserve full-catalog model rankings ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

Recommended workflow: create chronological inner tuning windows exclusively within permitted training histories; fit on earlier interactions and score later training-only targets, with preprocessing and sampling restricted to information available at each cutoff. Use rolling-origin windows if affordable, freeze architecture, hyperparameters, and stopping rules, then retrain on the original training split. Preserve benchmark splits and leave held-out test labels to the host. Temporal evaluation supports future-prediction assessment ([Time to Split](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748164)). Previously inspected benchmark validation results remain exploratory; training-only retuning cannot retroactively make them independent confirmation.
